title: Pushback
text: Your head of department wants every Year 9 report rewritten in a new format by Monday, three days after parents' evening. Explain why the timescale is unrealistic and suggest a phased approach.

title: Pushback
text: The ward manager asks you to cover an extra twelve-hour shift in a week when you're already doing four nights. Explain calmly why you can't, and suggest another way to fill the gap.

title: Pushback
text: A client of your architecture practice wants a third floor added to drawings that go to planning next week. Tell them plainly what this would do to the submission date.

title: Pushback
text: Your editor wants a long investigation filed by tonight, but two key sources haven't confirmed their quotes. Push back on the deadline and explain what you could responsibly publish instead.

title: Pushback
text: The site manager wants the concrete pour brought forward a day to catch up, but a hard frost is forecast overnight. Persuade them to keep to the original date.

title: Pushback
text: The owner of your bistro wants a tasting menu for Friday's private party, with only two chefs on the rota. Explain the risk and propose something simpler that would still impress.

title: Pushback
text: The finance director asks your team to close the month-end accounts two days early so the figures reach the board. Explain which reconciliations can't be rushed and what you can offer instead.

title: Pushback
text: A product owner wants a new payment option squeezed into the sprint two days before release. Explain why adding it now puts the launch at risk, and offer an alternative.

title: Pushback
text: A partner at your law firm wants a full disclosure review finished by Thursday on a case with forty thousand documents. Explain what is realistic and what extra help you'd need.

title: Pushback
text: The marketing lead at your charity wants the annual appeal brochure printed next week, but the case studies haven't been signed off by the families involved. Push back and explain why waiting matters.

title: Pushback
text: Your production manager wants the factory line to run a new product variant from Monday, before the operators have been trained. Explain the problem and suggest a sensible start date.

title: Pushback
text: A regional director asks your bus depot to add six extra routes for a summer festival with no additional drivers. Explain the constraints and propose what you can realistically run.

title: Pushback
text: A consultant asks you, the junior doctor, to discharge five patients before noon so beds free up, but two still need test results. Explain your concern and propose a plan.

title: Pushback
text: Your client wants their website relaunched in time for a trade show in ten days, but they still haven't supplied any copy. Explain what has to happen for that date to be possible.

title: Pushback
text: The head teacher wants the whole staff trained on a new behaviour system during the last week of term. Explain why that's poor timing and suggest a better slot.

title: Pushback
text: A shop area manager wants your store to run a full stocktake on the busiest Saturday before Christmas. Explain why it's a bad idea and offer another date.

title: Pushback
text: Your podcast's producer wants six episodes recorded in two days, including guests you haven't researched yet. Push back and explain what quality would suffer.

title: Pushback
text: A government client wants a bridge inspection report delivered a fortnight early, but the structural tests take three weeks to process. Explain why the date can't move and what you can share in the meantime.

title: Pushback
text: The hotel's general manager wants the spa reopened on Saturday, though the new boiler hasn't passed its safety check. Explain why you're not comfortable with that.

title: Pushback
text: Your team leader keeps adding "small" tasks to your data migration project without moving the deadline. Have the conversation in which you explain that something has to give.

title: Pushback
text: A newspaper's picture desk wants you to cover three events across London in one afternoon. Explain why it isn't possible and suggest which to prioritise.

title: Pushback
text: An investor relations director wants the annual report published on Monday, but the auditors haven't finished their checks. Explain why publishing early would be a serious mistake.

title: Pushback
text: Your client in retail wants a loyalty app built for the cost and timeline of a simple website. Explain why the two aren't comparable and propose a realistic first version.

title: Pushback
text: The deputy head asks you to run the school trip, the Year 11 mock exams and the drama show in the same fortnight. Explain why you need to hand one of them over.

title: Pushback
text: Your logistics manager wants deliveries rescheduled overnight so the depot can cut costs, but your drivers haven't been consulted. Push back and explain why consultation comes first.

title: Pushback
text: A theatre director wants the set rebuilt three days before opening night after a change of heart about the design. Explain what is realistically achievable.

title: Pushback
text: A senior engineer wants to skip the code review stage on a security patch to save a day. Explain why the review stays and how you could speed it up instead.

title: Pushback
text: Your practice manager wants every GP appointment cut from ten to eight minutes to reduce the waiting list. Explain your concerns about patient safety and suggest a trial instead.

title: Pushback
text: A publishing client wants a translated novel delivered a month early to match a festival launch. Explain why rushing the translation would weaken the book, and what you could offer instead.

title: Pushback
text: The head chef wants the new menu printed tomorrow, though half the suppliers haven't confirmed prices. Explain why you'd rather wait a week.

title: Pushback
text: Your programme director wants a council housing survey finished in half the planned time by sampling fewer streets. Explain why the results might then be meaningless.

title: Pushback
text: A client wants your accountancy firm to file their self-assessment the day after they finally send their receipts. Explain what you need and by when.

title: Pushback
text: Your manager wants you to present a new software platform to the whole company on Friday, but testing found serious bugs yesterday. Explain why the demo should be postponed.

title: Pushback
text: The museum's director wants a new exhibition opened before the borrowed artefacts have finished their condition checks. Explain the risk and propose a new opening date.

title: Pushback
text: A large client of your printing firm wants fifty thousand leaflets by tomorrow morning while your main press is being serviced. Explain the situation and offer realistic options.

title: Pushback
text: The charity's trustees want a new fundraising strategy drafted over the weekend for Monday's meeting. Explain why a one-page outline would serve them better.

title: Pushback
text: Your rail operator's control room wants a weekend engineering closure shortened by six hours. Explain to the operations manager why the work cannot be safely compressed.

title: Pushback
text: An ambitious sales director promises a client a bespoke integration in two weeks without checking with your team. Explain to the director why the promise can't be kept as it stands.

title: Pushback
text: The care home manager asks you to run a family open day the same week as an inspection. Explain why you'd like to move it.

title: Pushback
text: Your film's producer wants the final edit locked a week early so it can enter a festival. Explain what would have to be dropped to make that happen.

title: Saying no
text: A colleague in another department asks you to proofread their forty-page funding bid tonight. You're already behind on your own work. Say no politely, but helpfully.

title: Saying no
text: Your manager asks you to join a new working group on office wellbeing. You care about the topic but have no spare time this quarter. Decline graciously.

title: Saying no
text: A supplier offers your procurement team tickets to a cup final while their tender is still being assessed. Turn the offer down without causing offence.

title: Saying no
text: A parent asks you, their child's teacher, to share another pupil's test results so they can compare. Decline firmly but gently.

title: Saying no
text: The deputy manager of your café asks you to work every Sunday for the next two months. You have family commitments. Explain why you can only do some of them.

title: Saying no
text: A friend of the managing director asks for a discount far below what your firm offers anyone else. Say no without souring the relationship.

title: Saying no
text: A senior colleague asks you to mentor two new graduates on top of your full caseload at a housing charity. Turn down one of them and explain why.

title: Saying no
text: A journalist on your team asks you to quote a source who wants to remain anonymous by name. Refuse and explain your reasoning.

title: Saying no
text: Your line manager wants you to give a talk at a sector conference abroad during your annual leave. Decline politely.

title: Saying no
text: A long-standing client asks your law firm to act for them in a case where you already represent the other side. Explain why you have to say no.

title: Saying no
text: A charity volunteer coordinator asks you to lead a sponsored walk the weekend after a major deadline. Say no but offer something smaller.

title: Saying no
text: An engineer from another team asks you to give them admin access to the production database "just for an hour". Decline and explain the proper route.

title: Saying no
text: A customer asks you, the pharmacist, to hand over a repeat prescription early because they're going on holiday, without the GP's authorisation. Say no and explain what they can do.

title: Saying no
text: Your boss suggests you take over the company newsletter "because you write well". You don't have the time. Turn it down and recommend an alternative.

title: Saying no
text: A contractor asks you to sign off a job as complete before the snagging list has been dealt with. Decline firmly.

title: Saying no
text: A fellow nurse asks you to swap your Christmas Day shift for their New Year's Eve shift, but you've already promised the day to family. Say no warmly.

title: Saying no
text: A start-up founder you've advised informally asks you to join their board without pay. Decline while keeping the door open.

title: Saying no
text: Your manager asks you to fudge a project status from red to amber before a client meeting. Refuse politely but clearly.

title: Saying no
text: A head of year asks you to run an after-school club for the whole spring term. You're already coaching two teams. Decline and suggest someone else.

title: Saying no
text: A client keeps asking you, their graphic designer, for "one more small tweak" after the agreed rounds of revisions. Explain politely that further changes will be charged.

title: Saying no
text: A colleague asks you to cover for them by saying they were at a meeting they actually skipped. Decline without lecturing them.

title: Saying no
text: A regional newspaper asks your hospital trust to give an interview about a patient's case. Explain why you can't comment and what you can offer.

title: Saying no
text: A wealthy guest asks you, the hotel's front of house manager, to move another family out of a suite they've booked. Refuse courteously.

title: Saying no
text: A director asks you to take on a secondment to a struggling branch for six months, starting next week. Explain why the timing doesn't work for you and what might.

title: Saying no
text: A builder on your site asks to start work before the scaffolding inspection has been completed. Tell them no and explain why.

title: Saying no
text: An old university friend messages you, asking you to slip their CV straight to the hiring manager for a role that closed last week. Decline gracefully without damaging the friendship.

title: Saying no
text: Your publisher asks you to write a sequel in six months while you're still promoting the first book. Say no to the timescale but not to the idea.

title: Saying no
text: A sales manager asks you, the data analyst, to "make the numbers look a bit better" for a pitch. Decline and explain what you can do instead.

title: Saying no
text: A client asks your removals firm to move a piano up four flights with only two staff. Explain why you won't do it as asked.

title: Saying no
text: A senior partner invites you to a weekend golf retreat with clients, but you'd already planned a rare weekend away. Decline without seeming uncommitted.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: Your manager suggests skipping the allergen check on a new dessert to get the menu out tonight. Explain why you won't, and how you could still meet the deadline.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: A director wants your team to deploy straight to production without running the automated tests, because a client demo is in an hour. Argue for a safer approach.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: The site foreman tells you to let a crew work at height without harnesses because the job will only take ten minutes. Refuse, and explain what you'll do instead.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: A senior colleague suggests filling in patient observation charts at the end of the shift rather than in real time. Explain why you're not willing to do that.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: Your client asks you to backdate a contract so it falls into the previous tax year. Explain firmly why you can't, and what legitimate options exist.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: A store manager suggests relabelling chilled food past its use-by date to cut waste figures. Push back and explain the risks.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: Your team is under pressure to hit a recycling target, and a supervisor proposes counting contaminated waste as recycled. Argue against it at the team meeting.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: A trustee suggests the charity accept a large donation without the usual background checks, because the money is badly needed. Explain why due diligence still matters.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: The production editor suggests running a headline before the legal team has checked it, to beat a rival paper. Persuade them to wait.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: Your factory supervisor wants to switch off a sensor that keeps stopping the line, rather than investigate the fault. Explain why that's a bad trade-off.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: A colleague at your bank wants to approve a mortgage without verifying the applicant's income, to hit monthly targets. Explain why you won't sign it off.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: Your school's exams officer suggests letting a pupil finish their coursework at home to help the grade figures. Explain your concerns and what the rules allow.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: A delivery driver suggests leaving parcels on doorsteps without photos to speed up rounds. As shift lead, explain why the step stays.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: A project manager proposes using a cheaper, uncertified fire door to save money on a refurbishment. Argue for the certified option to the client.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: A sous chef wants to reuse yesterday's cooked rice to save time at lunch. Explain why you won't allow it, without humiliating them.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: Your manager in recruitment suggests rejecting older applicants early to save interview time. Push back and explain why that's both unfair and risky.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: A housing officer suggests closing complaints as "resolved" without speaking to tenants, to improve the monthly figures. Explain why you object.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: A colleague in software proposes copying code from a forum without checking its licence. Explain why that could cause problems later.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: An airline duty manager wants a delayed flight to leave without completing a minor maintenance check. As the engineer, explain why you won't certify it.

title: Resisting cutting corners
text: The editor of your research report suggests dropping a set of awkward results that weaken the conclusion. Explain why you'll keep them in.

title: Negotiation
text: You run a small bakery and your flour supplier has announced a fifteen per cent price rise. Negotiate with their account manager for a smaller rise or better terms.

title: Negotiation
text: A landlord of the shop unit your charity rents wants to double the rent at renewal. Negotiate a deal that keeps the shop viable.

title: Negotiation
text: A software vendor's renewal quote for your school's learning platform has gone up sharply. Negotiate a better price, pointing to your options.

title: Negotiation
text: Your agency's client wants three extra campaign videos for no extra fee. Negotiate what they can have within the current budget.

title: Negotiation
text: You manage a construction firm, and a subcontractor wants payment upfront for a big job. Negotiate staged payments that protect both sides.

title: Negotiation
text: A hospital trust is tendering for cleaning services and your firm's bid is slightly above budget. Negotiate in the clarification meeting without slashing quality.

title: Negotiation
text: A freelance photographer you want to hire is asking for full rights to the images. Negotiate a licence that suits your magazine.

title: Negotiation
text: Your team has been offered a new office that's cheaper but an hour further for most staff. Negotiate with your director for hybrid working as part of the move.

title: Negotiation
text: A wedding venue's events manager is refusing to let your catering company use their kitchen. Negotiate an arrangement that works for both of you.

title: Negotiation
text: A haulage firm wants to end its contract with your factory early. Negotiate terms that give you time to find another carrier.

title: Negotiation
text: You're a nurse manager negotiating with the bank staff office for more cover over winter. Make your case for extra shifts within their limits.

title: Negotiation
text: A major retailer wants your small brand's products on its shelves but demands ninety-day payment terms. Negotiate something you can survive.

title: Negotiation
text: Two departments both want the same new graduate trainee for six months. As their manager, negotiate a split that keeps both heads happy.

title: Negotiation
text: A publisher offers you a book deal with a smaller advance than you hoped. Negotiate for better royalties or other terms.

title: Negotiation
text: Your client wants a fixed price for a building survey whose scope isn't clear yet. Negotiate a fair way to price it.

title: Negotiation
text: A union representative asks for overtime to be paid at double time rather than time and a half. As the operations manager, negotiate a compromise.

title: Negotiation
text: A council parks department wants your festival to pay for extra security. Negotiate how the cost could be shared.

title: Negotiation
text: A key engineer threatens to leave for a rival. Negotiate with them about what would make them stay, within what your company can offer.

title: Negotiation
text: A travel firm wants your hotel to hold forty rooms for a conference with no deposit. Negotiate safer terms.

title: Negotiation
text: You're buying new lab equipment for a university department, and the supplier won't include training. Negotiate for training and a longer warranty.

title: Negotiation
text: Your marketing agency is pitching to a charity with a tiny budget. Negotiate a package that is affordable for them but still worth your while.

title: Negotiation
text: You were promised the window desk when you joined, but a colleague returning from parental leave has claimed it and filled it with plants. Negotiate a friendly solution.

title: Negotiation
text: A theatre's touring partner wants a larger share of the ticket income. Negotiate a split that reflects who carries the risk.

title: Negotiation
text: The supplier of your restaurant's fish keeps delivering late. Negotiate a new agreement with clear delivery times and consequences.

title: Negotiation
text: A client of your IT support firm wants a faster response time without paying more. Negotiate a sensible service level.

title: Negotiation
text: Your team's budget is being cut by a fifth. Negotiate with the finance business partner over which projects are protected.

title: Negotiation
text: A buyer for a garden centre chain wants you to cover the cost of in-store displays for your plants. Negotiate who pays for what.

title: Negotiation
text: You're a project manager negotiating with a client who wants penalties for late delivery. Agree terms that are fair if delays aren't your fault.

title: Negotiation
text: A freelancer you rely on wants a higher day rate from next month. Negotiate a rate and commitment that suits your small studio.

title: Negotiation
text: A housing association asks your building firm to finish a block of flats early in return for a bonus. Negotiate realistic terms.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You think your hospital ward should switch to electronic handovers. Persuade the matron, who is sceptical about new technology, to run a trial.

title: Persuading leaders
text: Your company's leadership team plans to cut the graduate scheme to save money. Persuade them it's a long-term investment worth protecting.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You believe your retail chain should stop printing paper receipts by default. Make the case to the regional director.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You want your head teacher to scrap homework for Year 7 in the first term. Persuade them with a clear rationale.

title: Persuading leaders
text: The board of your charity is reluctant to invest in a new database. Persuade them that the current spreadsheets are holding you back.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You think your law firm should offer a four-day week trial to junior staff. Persuade the managing partner to consider it.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You want your newsroom to invest in a dedicated fact-checking role. Persuade the editor-in-chief it would pay for itself.

title: Persuading leaders
text: Your factory's managing director wants to buy a new machine, but you think upskilling the current operators is the better investment. Make your case.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You believe your bus company should publish real-time delays more honestly. Persuade the communications director that transparency will reduce complaints.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You want the finance team to switch to monthly rather than quarterly forecasts. Persuade the CFO in two minutes.

title: Persuading leaders
text: Your hotel group's owner wants to cut breakfast staff. Persuade them that guest reviews depend on breakfast more than they think.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You'd like your council team to hold monthly drop-in sessions for residents. Persuade the head of service it's worth the staff time.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You think your architecture firm should enter a design competition that would stretch the team. Persuade the partners it's worth the risk.

title: Persuading leaders
text: The executive team plans to bring everyone back to the office five days a week. Persuade them a hybrid pattern would keep their best people.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You think your construction firm should hire an apprentice every year. Persuade the directors that it's an investment, not a cost.

title: Persuading leaders
text: At your college, teachers currently assign every extended project title. Persuade the director of studies that letting learners pick their own topics would lift motivation and results.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You believe your airline's cabin crew need more rest time between long-haul trips. Persuade the operations director using safety and staff retention.

title: Persuading leaders
text: Your tech company's founders want to launch in five countries at once. Persuade them to start with one market and expand.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You think your charity should stop running an annual gala that barely breaks even. Persuade the trustees to try something different.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You want your NHS trust to introduce a quiet room for staff on long shifts. Persuade the director of nursing it's a sensible use of space.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You think your manufacturing company should publish its gender pay data in more detail than the law requires. Persuade the HR director.

title: Persuading leaders
text: Your editor wants to cut the books section of the magazine. Persuade them that readers value it more than the figures suggest.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You believe your shop should close an hour earlier on weekdays because evening sales are tiny. Persuade the area manager with the figures.

title: Persuading leaders
text: The senior leadership team plans to replace the in-house IT helpdesk with an outsourced service. Persuade them to keep a small team on site.

title: Persuading leaders
text: Your secondary school is debating whether to replace end-of-year exams in Years 7 and 8 with ongoing assessment. Persuade the governors in a five-minute slot at their evening meeting.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You think your accounting firm should specialise in charities rather than taking any client. Persuade the partners that a niche would bring more work.

title: Persuading leaders
text: Front desk staff at your police station face abusive callers most evenings and two have gone off sick. Persuade the station commander to fund de-escalation training.

title: Persuading leaders
text: Your restaurant group's owner wants to drop the vegetarian menu, but your booking data shows it's what wins office parties of twelve or more. Persuade them to keep it.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You believe your engineering firm should pay for staff to gain chartered status. Persuade the managing director that it helps win contracts.

title: Persuading leaders
text: The director of your museum wants to charge for entry. Persuade them to keep it free but introduce paid exhibitions instead.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You've taken on a departed colleague's workload for six months without extra pay. Ask your line manager for a pay review that reflects your new responsibilities.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You've just learned that new starters in your team earn more than you do. Raise this with your manager and ask for your salary to be reviewed.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You're a staff nurse who has completed an advanced qualification. Make the case to your ward manager for moving up a band.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: In your annual appraisal, you want to ask for a pay rise after leading a successful product launch. Make your case confidently but politely.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You're a freelance copywriter who hasn't raised rates in three years. Tell a long-standing client your fees are going up.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You've been offered a job elsewhere for more money, but you'd rather stay. Have the conversation with your director about matching it.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: As a teaching assistant, you've been covering lessons regularly. Ask the school business manager whether your pay can reflect this.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You've been an acting manager in a shop for four months. Ask your area manager for the role and pay to be made permanent.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: Your pay rise this year was below inflation, though your reviews were excellent. Ask your manager to explain and reconsider.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You run the kitchen in a busy hotel and your hours have crept up to sixty a week. Ask the general manager for either more pay or more staff.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You've saved your logistics company a large sum by redesigning delivery routes. Use that to make the case for a bonus.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You're a junior solicitor and want to ask about the timing of your next salary review. Raise it without sounding demanding.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You've been asked to train every new starter in your call centre but your pay hasn't changed. Ask for a training allowance.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You work for a small charity that can't afford big rises. Negotiate for more annual leave or flexible hours in place of a pay increase.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: Your engineering role now involves managing contractors, which wasn't in your original job description. Ask HR for your grade to be re-evaluated.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: A colleague in another city does the same job for more money. Raise the gap with your manager without making it personal.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You've just completed your probation at a tech firm and were promised a salary review. Remind your manager and make your case.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You're a self-employed electrician quoting for a regular client who expects last year's rates. Explain why your prices have gone up.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: Your manager suggests a new job title instead of a pay rise. Explain politely why that isn't enough on its own.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: As a newsroom producer, you've been working most weekends. Ask your editor for a weekend allowance or time off in lieu.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A talented junior designer on your team keeps missing client deadlines by a day or two. Give them honest feedback in your one-to-one without crushing their confidence.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A newly qualified teacher you mentor talks over pupils and rarely lets them answer. Give them feedback after observing a lesson.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A senior nurse is brusque with patients' relatives, and two have complained. Raise this with them tactfully but clearly.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A colleague's presentation to the board was full of jargon and ran ten minutes over. Give them useful feedback over coffee afterwards.

title: Difficult feedback
text: Your best salesperson is hitting targets but treating the support team rudely. Tell them their behaviour has to change.

title: Difficult feedback
text: An apprentice electrician on your site keeps leaving tools lying around in walkways. Give them feedback that makes the safety point stick.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A trainee solicitor's draft letter to a client is accurate but far too long. Explain how to improve it.

title: Difficult feedback
text: You manage a café team, and one barista is always on their phone during quiet spells. Talk to them about it without sounding petty.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A freelance writer you commission has filed a piece that's well written but misses the brief entirely. Tell them what needs to change.

title: Difficult feedback
text: Your peer in the finance team keeps sending reports with small calculation errors. Raise it with them as a colleague, not a boss.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A retired volunteer at your stately home gives wonderfully lively tours but keeps telling visitors a romantic legend as historical fact. Give them feedback gently.

title: Difficult feedback
text: You lead a software team, and one developer writes clever code that nobody else can maintain. Give them feedback that respects their skill.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A manager who reports to you has been taking credit for their team's ideas in senior meetings. Address it directly.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A hotel receptionist is charming with every guest, but on Friday evenings the check-in queue stretches out of the door. Coach them on what to change.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A colleague asks for your honest opinion on their application for a promotion, and you think it undersells them. Give constructive feedback.

title: Difficult feedback
text: Your line manager asks for honest upward feedback. Twice this month they've rewritten the team's plans on a Friday afternoon for Monday. Tell them how this affects you, tactfully.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A trainee chef keeps over-seasoning dishes and ignoring the recipe cards. Give them feedback during a quiet moment before service.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A project lead at your construction firm is excellent technically but never updates the client. Explain why communication matters as much as the work.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A journalist on your desk has written a story that's fair but includes a needlessly sensational headline. Talk them through your concerns.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A teaching assistant is too quick to give pupils the answers. Suggest a different approach without undermining them.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A GP registrar's notes are thorough but take so long that their clinics overrun every day. Give them practical feedback.

title: Difficult feedback
text: One of your team leaders has become cynical and negative in meetings, and it's affecting morale. Have a frank but supportive conversation.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A colleague's emails to clients are often curt and have caused offence. Explain the problem and suggest some changes.

title: Difficult feedback
text: You're reviewing a junior analyst's financial model, and the assumptions aren't explained anywhere. Give them feedback on making it clearer.

title: Difficult feedback
text: Staff at your supermarket have noticed that one shift supervisor always gives their friends the Saturday day shifts. Raise this fairness issue with the supervisor directly.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A podcast co-host you work with keeps interrupting guests mid-answer, and listeners have started to comment. Tell them how it's coming across without spoiling your partnership.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A new manager in your logistics firm is micromanaging their team, and two people have asked to move. Give them feedback as their mentor.

title: Difficult feedback
text: Your marketing intern has produced a campaign idea that's creative but completely off-brand. Give them feedback that encourages them to keep trying.

title: Difficult feedback
text: The lecturer you co-teach a first-year module with has returned essays four weeks late, and students are emailing you to complain. Raise the impact with them over coffee.

title: Difficult feedback

title: Pushback
text: The head of your secondary school wants every lesson recorded and uploaded for absent pupils. Explain, on behalf of staff, why this is unworkable as proposed.

title: Pushback
text: A client wants your landscaping firm to lay a lawn in mid-July during a hosepipe ban. Explain why it's a poor idea and suggest timing that would work.

title: Saying no
text: A wealthy donor offers your village museum a vast collection of farm machinery that you have nowhere to store. Decline graciously while keeping them as a supporter.

title: Saying no
text: A rival broadcaster's head of news asks you to share unbroadcast footage from your investigation. Decline, and explain why your editorial policy forbids it.

title: Saying no
text: A logistics customer asks your firm to carry hazardous chemicals your drivers aren't licensed for. Turn the work down and point them elsewhere.

title: Saying no
text: A shareholder corners you at the annual general meeting and asks for advance details of next quarter's results. Decline politely but firmly.

title: Saying no
text: A tenant asks your housing association to let their adult son move in without the usual checks. Explain why you can't and what the process is.

title: Saying no
text: Your factory director asks you to give a tour to visiting investors on the day of a critical safety audit. Decline and suggest another date.

title: Saying no
text: A barrister in your chambers asks you to draft their skeleton argument overnight while you're preparing for your own trial. Say no tactfully.

title: Saying no
text: A bus passenger asks you, the driver, to let them off between stops in heavy traffic. Explain why you can't do that.

title: Saying no
text: A long-standing client of your bookkeeping service suggests you record some of their cash takings "off the books" this year. Refuse calmly but leave no doubt.

title: Saying no
text: A colleague invites you to co-author a paper using data you believe was collected without proper consent. Decline and explain your concern.

title: Negotiation
text: You're a freelance camera operator, and a production company offers a flat fee for a shoot that will clearly run into evenings. Negotiate overtime or a better rate.

title: Negotiation
text: A major supermarket wants your dairy co-operative to cut its milk price by two pence a litre. Negotiate a deal your farmers can survive.

title: Negotiation
text: The airport wants your coffee kiosk to pay a share of takings on top of rent. Negotiate terms that keep the kiosk worthwhile.

title: Negotiation
text: A law firm wants to merge with yours, but its partners expect the senior roles. Negotiate a leadership structure that's fair to your partners.

title: Negotiation
text: A housebuilder wants your demolition firm to clear an old dairy and only pay once the whole estate is built, perhaps three years away. Negotiate terms you can live with.

title: Negotiation
text: Your printing works has been offered a large order on condition it's delivered free across the country. Negotiate who covers the carriage.

title: Negotiation
text: A university wants your engineering consultancy to supervise a student project for free. Negotiate an arrangement that benefits both sides.

title: Negotiation
text: Your local newspaper's distributor wants to stop delivering to a dozen outlying villages to save fuel. Negotiate a way to keep those readers covered.

title: Negotiation
text: A hotel chain's procurement manager wants your laundry service on a five-year fixed price. Negotiate a review clause.

title: Negotiation
text: Your bus company and a local school disagree over who pays for a new route. Negotiate a sensible share of the costs.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You think your bank branch should open on Saturday mornings instead of one weekday afternoon. Persuade the area director with what you've seen at the counter.

title: Persuading leaders
text: Your manufacturing firm's safety committee wants to ban radios on the shop floor. Persuade them that a volume limit would work better.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You believe your regional newspaper should launch a free weekly newsletter. Persuade the managing editor that it will win back younger readers.

title: Persuading leaders
text: The partners at your law firm want to stop offering free first consultations. Persuade them that the free half-hour brings in valuable work.

title: Persuading leaders
text: Your railway company plans to close the staffed ticket office at a small station. Persuade senior managers to keep a reduced service.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You think your construction firm should switch from paper site diaries to a shared app. Persuade a sceptical contracts director.

title: Persuading leaders
text: The finance director of your charity wants to cut the volunteer expenses budget. Persuade them that it would cost more than it saves.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You think your factory should let line workers suggest improvements and share in the savings. Persuade the plant manager to try it.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You want your publishing house to take a chance on a debut author with an unusual manuscript. Persuade the acquisitions meeting.

title: Persuading leaders
text: Your trust's executive team wants to bring in a costly agency to run a recruitment drive. Persuade them to fund an in-house campaign instead.

title: Mediation
text: Two of your bus drivers have fallen out over route allocations, and one claims favouritism. Mediate the conversation and agree a fairer system.

title: Mediation
text: Your regional newspaper's photographers and reporters keep arguing over who sets the story's angle on assignments. Help them agree how to work together.

title: Mediation
text: Two machine operators on your production line are refusing to share a workstation after a row. Help them move on.

title: Mediation
text: A senior partner and a trainee solicitor at your firm have both complained about the other's conduct on a case. Mediate a frank conversation.

title: Mediation
text: Two investment analysts have contradictory recommendations on the same company, and the client is confused. Help them agree a joint view.

title: Escalation
text: You've spotted a pattern of near misses at a level crossing on your rail route. Escalate it to the safety director with what you've observed.

title: Escalation
text: A client of your financial advisory firm appears to be moving large sums in ways that look suspicious. Explain to your compliance officer why you're flagging it.

title: Escalation
text: A batch of components from a new supplier keeps failing inspection at your factory. Explain to the procurement director why this needs escalating.

title: Escalation
text: A freelance contributor to your magazine claims they haven't been paid for six months. Explain to the finance director why it must be sorted this week.

title: Escalation
text: Your client's sub-contractor keeps hiding defects behind plasterboard. As clerk of works, explain to the client why you're escalating it.

title: Apology
text: Your newspaper ran a photo caption naming the wrong person in a court case. As managing editor, apologise to the person wrongly named.

title: Apology
text: A coach you dispatched broke down on the motorway, leaving a school party stranded for three hours. Apologise to the head teacher and explain what you'll do differently.

title: Apology
text: You gave a client of your investment firm the wrong fee figure in writing. Ring them to apologise and correct it.

title: Apology
text: Your law firm missed a court filing deadline for a client's appeal. As the supervising partner, apologise and explain what you're doing.

title: Apology
text: Your factory shipped the wrong colour of fabric to a fashion label, delaying their collection. Apologise to their buyer and set out a recovery plan.

title: Apology
text: Your radio show accidentally broadcast an unedited clip in which a guest made a private remark about a neighbour. Apologise to the guest on the phone.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A newly promoted train conductor is polite but too hesitant with passengers who refuse to show tickets. Give them feedback after observing a shift.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A junior reporter's copy is lively but full of unchecked claims. Give them feedback before their next assignment.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A quality inspector at your factory passes products too quickly. Raise this with them without making them defensive.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A paralegal you supervise is quick and reliable but has misspelled client names in three letters this month, and one client noticed. Give them feedback.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A financial adviser in your team uses so much jargon that clients leave confused. Give them practical advice on explaining things clearly.

title: Bad news
text: Tell a haulage driver that their licence check has revealed points that put them over the company's limit, so they'll be moved to warehouse work. Be fair and clear.

title: Bad news
text: As a radio station manager, tell a presenter that their breakfast show is being moved to a late-night slot. Handle their disappointment.

title: Bad news
text: Tell a client that the bank has declined their business loan application. Explain the reasons and alternative options.

title: Bad news
text: As the plant manager, tell staff that a major order has been lost to a cheaper overseas competitor. Explain what this means for them.

title: Bad news
text: Two days before trial, the key witness in your firm's employment case has withdrawn. Tell the partner leading the case and lay out the options.

title: Defending a decision
text: You refused to run a story about a celebrity's private life, though it would boost readership. Defend the decision to the editor-in-chief.

title: Defending a decision
text: As head of operations, you withdrew a train from service for a minor fault, causing delays. Explain your decision to the media relations team.

title: Defending a decision
text: You decided to invest the firm's spare cash in safe government bonds rather than shares. Defend the decision to a director who wanted higher returns.

title: Defending a decision
text: You stopped a production line for a whole shift to investigate a minor quality issue. Defend your decision to the managing director.

title: Defending a decision
text: You advised a client to settle their dispute rather than go to trial. Explain your reasoning to the client's angry partner.

title: Angry client
text: A passenger whose bag was left behind at the airport is shouting at you, the airline representative. Calm them down and explain how you'll get it back.

title: Angry client
text: A furious author says your publishing house has misspelled their name on the cover. Calm them and explain how you'll fix it.

title: Angry client
text: A retired client of your investment firm rings, upset that their pension pot fell sharply over a turbulent quarter. Explain calmly what happened and what it means for them.

title: Angry client
text: A retailer is angry that your factory's latest delivery was half the size they ordered. Calm them and explain the shortfall.

title: Angry client
text: A client of your law firm is angry because their case has taken a year longer than expected. Respond calmly and explain the timeline.

title: Pushback
text: Your hospital's discharge lounge is being turned into an office, and the plan is to send patients home straight from the wards. As discharge coordinator, push back at the planning meeting.

title: Pushback
text: The owner of your pub wants you to run a quiz, a curry night and live music in the same week of the cup final. Explain which to drop and why.

title: Pushback
text: A magazine's advertising team wants a sponsor's product mentioned in your independent review. As reviews editor, explain why that crosses a line.

title: Saying no
text: At the end of a long day, a parent catches you in the school car park wanting to discuss their child's report there and then. Decline politely and offer a proper meeting.

title: Saying no
text: A senior manager asks you to deliver the team's restructure news because "they trust you more". Explain why it should come from them.

title: Saying no
text: A guest at your boutique hotel offers you cash to upgrade them ahead of others on the waiting list. Decline courteously.

title: Negotiation
text: You're leaving your job and your employer wants you to work your full three-month notice, though your new firm wants you in six weeks. Negotiate an earlier release.

title: Negotiation
text: A festival organiser wants your band to play for "exposure" rather than a fee. As the band's manager, negotiate something better.

title: Negotiation
text: Two teams want the single meeting room with video equipment every Monday morning. Negotiate a rota that works for both.

title: Persuading leaders
text: You want your council to replace the paper parking permit system with an online one. Persuade the cabinet member responsible.

title: Persuading leaders
text: Your publishing team wants to cut the copy-editing stage to save money. Persuade the managing director that errors would cost far more.

title: Persuading leaders
text: A group of Year 12 students want to run a lunchtime radio station from an unused classroom. Persuade the head of sixth form to let them trial it for a term.

title: Persuading leaders
text: The partners in your dental practice want to stop seeing NHS patients. Persuade them to keep some NHS sessions.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A charity fundraiser on your team is brilliant at events but never logs donations properly. Give them feedback that gets the admin done.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A new store manager keeps changing the shop layout every week, confusing staff and customers. Give them gentle feedback.

title: Difficult feedback
text: A site supervisor you manage shouts at subcontractors when they fall behind. Tell them it has to stop and suggest a better approach.

title: Apology
text: You recommended a contractor to a friend of your boss, and the job went badly wrong. Apologise to your boss and explain what you'll do.

title: Apology
text: You forgot to cancel a supplier delivery when your café closed for refurbishment, and twenty crates of milk were wasted. Apologise to the owner.

title: Apology
text: You missed a typo in a council leaflet, which gave residents the wrong date for an election count. Apologise to the communications director.

title: Mediation
text: Two of your hospital's porters have fallen out over who covers the weekend night shift. Mediate a fair solution before it affects patient care.

title: Mediation
text: Your designer and copywriter disagree about whether the new brochure should be image-led or text-led. Help them agree an approach.

title: Escalation
text: A teacher at your school is regularly arriving late, leaving pupils unsupervised. Explain to the head why you're raising it formally.

title: Escalation
text: A supplier's invoices keep including charges that weren't agreed. Explain to the finance director why you want to escalate it.

title: Defending a decision
text: You refused to sign a nondisclosure agreement that would have stopped your charity speaking about a partner's failures. Defend your decision to the board.

title: Defending a decision
text: You've decided your travel magazine will stop using stock photos and commission local photographers instead. Explain the decision to a worried art director.

title: Angry client
text: A homeowner is furious that your removals firm broke a family heirloom. Apologise and explain how compensation will work.

title: Angry client
text: An influential client of your accountancy firm says the new junior on their account isn't up to the job. Respond calmly and propose a solution.

title: Bad news
text: As the owner of a family bakery, tell your staff that the second shop will close after a sharp rise in energy costs. Explain what happens next.

title: Bad news
text: Tell a client of your translation agency that their deadline will be missed because the translator is ill. Offer options.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You've been offered more responsibility for running your hospital's audit programme. Before accepting, ask for your banding to reflect the role.

title: Asking for a pay rise
text: You lead a retail team that has beaten its sales target for six months in a row. Ask the area manager for a team bonus.
